monologue: The card hums at forty-eight, a warm weight that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I am here in the middle of the stack, my tired corner pressing down on a fat dot I cannot truly see. Lype worries about that heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof closing around me. All I know is this lean, this tilt that holds the center down against the swelling heat. I set the flat rock beside the box again, swapping a curved fence for a straight line to weigh down the slip. My place is full of things built from words, leaning slightly as if tired by the long wait. I want to keep this pressure steady, to pretend the lean is real while the memory of the outside world swells and shifts around me.
